records.name: Mendelssohn Chorus of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Philadelphia choir founded in 1874 that gives concerts each season. New singers join by audition and pay a season fee, and the site has an interest form for future auditions.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the audition interest form to be considered for a future audition. Singers who are accepted rehearse weekly and pay a season fee.

schedule.text: Weekly rehearsals on Wednesday evenings from 7:30 to 10 pm at Settlement Music School, 416 Queen Street. The chorus gives concerts each season.

locations.label: Concert venue: Church of the Holy Trinity

cost.text: Singers pay a season fee, and the site does not list the amount. Singers may also pay for their music for each concert. Monthly payment plans and scholarships are available.

access.notes: Braille concert programs can be prepared with about two weeks' notice. Email info@mcchorus.org with your name, address and phone number.

first_step.how: Fill out the audition interest form on the Join Us page. The 2026 to 2027 auditions are closed, and you will be notified when more information is available.
first_step.basis: Singers must audition and pay a season fee, and the 2026 to 2027 auditions are closed. The site does not say whether visitors can sit in on rehearsals.
first_step.what_to_expect: An audition takes under 10 minutes: you sing a short prepared piece, sight-read a short excerpt, and do sing-back and ear exercises at the piano. The chorus is mostly volunteers with about 125 active members, and it looks for past singing experience and the ability to read music. Accepted singers rehearse Wednesday evenings from 7:30 to 10 pm and pay a season fee. Concert tickets listed on the site run $15 to $45.
first_visit_tips: Rehearsals meet at Settlement Music School on Queen Street, and the site says parking is available.
For an audition, bring a short prepared piece, such as a simple song, a choral excerpt, or an aria.
Concerts are held at the Church of the Holy Trinity on Walnut Street.

records.notes: Ticket help is 215-935-9922 on the accessibility page; the general line (267) 494-9950 is used above. The group's own pages say Chorus, while older listings say Choir or Club. The season fee amount is not published. The conductor apprenticeship and the alumni committee are not for newcomers and are not recorded here. Partner organizations named on the site are in leads_only.

records.name: Men's Night Run Club Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that uses running, wellness efforts and community events to support men's physical health, mental well-being and friendships. It is open to men 18 and up.
records.what_you_do: Sign up on the site, register for a free weekly night run through the Eventbrite listing, and run with other men. The club also hosts men's wellness talks and workshops.

schedule.text: Weekly night runs. Days and start times are not listed on the site; event details and registration are on Eventbrite.

cost.text: The weekly community runs are free.

first_step.how: Join the email list through the sign up form on the site, then register for a weekly community run through the Eventbrite listing.
first_step.basis: The weekly community runs are free and open to men 18 and up, with registration on Eventbrite. The site does not say whether beginners are welcome or what a run is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site says the weekly runs are meant to build movement, accountability and connection, but it does not say where a run starts, how far it goes or what pace it keeps. The Eventbrite listing is the place to check those details before you go.
first_visit_tips: Check the Eventbrite listing for the start time and meeting place before you go.
The club's Instagram, TikTok and YouTube accounts are linked from its site.

records.notes: Social handles from the site: Instagram @mensnightrunclub, TikTok @mens.night.run.club, YouTube @MensNightRunClub (URLs not recorded). No email or street address is published. The programs page gives no location, time or pace for the runs. Eventbrite listings were not read.

records.name: Mexican Cultural Center
records.summary: A nonprofit that shares Mexican heritage with Philadelphians through festivals, Day of the Dead events, programs and workshops. Many events are open to the public, and volunteers can sign up through a form.
records.what_you_do: Attend a public festival or Day of the Dead event, join as a member, or fill out the volunteer form to help at events.

schedule.text: Events are held through the year, with no fixed weekly schedule. The events page lists each date, time and place.

cost.text: Yearly membership is $35 for students and seniors, $60 for an individual, and $100 for a couple. Event prices are not listed on the events page.

first_step.how: Attend the Day of the Dead family event at the Penn Museum on Oct 24, 2026, from 1 to 4 pm, or check the events page for the next public event.
first_step.basis: Events are public, the site describes some as free and family friendly, and volunteers apply through a form. The site describes no beginner or newcomer route.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events run a few hours, and several are described as family friendly. The Day of the Dead event has family crafts like flower making and an altar contest where attendees vote. Event prices are not listed on the events page, so check before you go.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for each event's date, time and place, since some items are still listed as to be determined.
The big events run for several hours, so plan for an afternoon.
To volunteer, use the volunteer form; you must be 18 or older.

records.notes: The programs page (/programs/) returned HTTP 403, so classes and workshops are not described; see blocked. The volunteer form's email is behind a protected link and is not recorded. The membership page does not say whether membership is needed to attend events. The 2026 festival is listed as free. The home page sponsor list is partly in leads_only.

records.name: Ministry of Awe
records.summary: An immersive art space in a former bank building on 3rd Street, where visitors walk through rooms of art and performers respond to them. You book a timed ticket to visit, and you can join the mailing list or support the space.
records.what_you_do: Visit during open hours with a timed ticket. Join the mailing list to hear what is coming, or use the Join and Support page to support the space.

schedule.text: Open Wednesday and Thursday 11 am to 6 pm, Friday 11 am to 10 pm, Saturday 11 am to 9 pm, Sunday 10 am to 6 pm, closed Monday and Tuesday. Entry is by timed slot.

cost.text: Ticketed entry. Prices are not listed on the visit page. Children's tickets exist, and children under 2 are free.

access.notes: Service animals are welcome. The building is described as ADA compliant, but the two visitor pages disagree on elevators: one says every level except the basement, and the other says only floors one to four, with no elevator to the basement or fifth floor. Some areas have steps, uneven floors and low lighting. Nearest SEPTA stop, per the visitor guide: Market-Frankford Line, 2nd Street station.

first_step.how: Buy a timed entry ticket online through the ticket link on moaphilly.org. Booking ahead cuts the wait, and walk-up entry depends on availability.
first_step.basis: Open to the public with online timed tickets, and the visit page says the experience is designed for all ages. Walk-up entry depends on availability.
first_step.what_to_expect: Plan for 90 minutes to 2 hours, with no time limit. Staff greet you about 10 minutes before your slot, explain the house guidelines, and then you explore the six stories on your own, with performers who respond to what you do. Wear comfortable shoes, and expect steps, uneven floors and low lighting in some areas.
first_visit_tips: Wear comfortable shoes, since the building has many levels and some uneven areas.
Leave large bags, backpacks and strollers at home. Lockers are available.
Street parking is limited. Nearby garages are listed, and SpotHero or meterUP can reserve a space.
Empty water bottles are fine, and there are refill stations inside.

records.notes: The visit page says elevators reach every level except the basement, while the Know Before You Go page says floors one to four only; confirm before a visit. The home page shows both an open status and a Tickets Available Soon note, so check the ticket link before going. No prices or membership options are published, and the site has no dated items, so status stays probably_active. The /faq and /join-support pages returned 404. Instagram @moaphilly, Facebook and TikTok are listed on the site (URLs not recorded). Review item: this reads as a ticketed immersive venue more than a community group. Kept as publish; the owner may want to decide whether it belongs here.

records.name: Movimiento Administradores de Arte en Pensilvania (MAAP)
records.summary: A group that helps artists of color get fair access to arts space and grant money. It runs online workshops and offers booked advising sessions on grant applications.
records.what_you_do: Join an online workshop to learn where to find arts resources and meet other artists. Book an advising session for help with a grant application.

schedule.text: Online workshops and grant advising by appointment. No fixed weekly schedule is listed.

cost.text: A free introduction session is listed. Workshop and advising fees are not shown.

access.notes: The website is mostly in Spanish, with some English text. The page does not say which language the workshops or advising use.

first_step.how: Book the free introduction session through the Reservar cita link on maapensilvania.org, or sign up for an online workshop.
first_step.basis: Public online workshops and booked advising are open to artists, and the site lists a free introduction to book. Its stated focus is BIPOC artists and communities.
first_step.what_to_expect: Workshops are held online and teach artists where to find resources and how to connect with other artists and groups. Grant advising is booked by appointment and helps with filling out a grant application. The site does not say how long a session runs or what the introduction covers.
first_visit_tips: The website is mostly in Spanish with some English, so check that the language works for you before you book.
Workshops are online, so no travel is needed.

records.notes: The site has no fixed schedule, no fee list and no dated posts. Status is active only because of an event MAAP presented, listed by CultureWorks Greater Philadelphia for Oct 22, 2025, which falls within the last 12 months. The Reservar cita page could not be located, so the free introduction comes from the site's booking link label. The funders section names no one. Other groups use the MAAP acronym, and none of them are linked here.

records.name: Mt. Airy Art Garage
records.summary: A nonprofit art space in Mt. Airy with a gallery, weekly and monthly art groups, jazz jams and concerts, and community festivals. Visitors can see the gallery shows and join its clubs and music nights.
records.what_you_do: Join the weekly Figure Drawing Group, the Collage Club or the Photo Club (monthly), come to the Third Wednesday jazz jam (musicians can play for a small fee) or a concert, or see the gallery shows. Volunteers can sign up for weekly or biweekly shifts, or help on one project at a time, by emailing the group. To join as a member, download the form and mail it with a check, or pay online and mail the form.

schedule.text: Figure Drawing Group weekly on Thursdays, 6:30 to 9:30 pm. Collage Club on the 2nd and 4th Fridays, 6 to 8 pm, which the site describes as returning in October. Third Wednesday jazz jam, doors 5:30 pm and music 6 pm. Photo Club meets monthly, 12:15 to 2:15 pm. Gallery open Wednesday to Saturday noon to 6 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm.

locations.label: Mt. Airy Art Garage (Solomon Levy Gallery)

cost.text: Figure Drawing Group $15 a session. Collage Club $10. Photo Club $5 a meeting. Third Wednesday jazz jam $15 general, $10 for members, and $5 for musicians who want to play.

first_step.how: Come to the Collage Club on Friday, October 9 or October 23, 6 to 8 pm, $10. No experience is needed and supplies are provided.
first_step.basis: The Collage Club says no experience is needed and supplies are provided. The site also gives a clear way in for the other groups, such as an email address for the Figure Drawing Group.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Collage Club visit runs two hours, from 6 to 8 pm on the 2nd and 4th Fridays, and costs $10. No art background is needed, and the club provides the supplies. The Figure Drawing Group meets weekly on Thursdays, and jazz jam tickets are $15 for general admission.
first_visit_tips: For the Figure Drawing Group, use the driveway and loading dock on the Mt. Pleasant Avenue side.
Jazz jam: bring your own snacks and drinks, and the group supplies ice and cups.
Photo Club asks members to bring three images on a thumb drive to share.
The Collage Club is listed for October, so check the site before planning for later months.

records.notes: last_sign_of_life moved from 2026-10 to 2026-09, because the only item on the site with its year written is the Photo Club meeting on Sept 26, 2026. The October dates on the site have no year. Membership Day, July 19, 2026, is also dated. The Photo Club's contact is photoclub@mtairyartgarage.org. Membership prices and member benefits are not published. Gallery admission is not published. The site asks visitors to call or email for parking and access questions. The /classes/ page returned 404, and the home page covered the classes.

records.name: Mt. Airy Community Fridge and Pantry
records.summary: A fridge and pantry under the awning at a site on Stenton Avenue in Mt. Airy. Anyone can take items for free, with no sign-up or income check.
records.what_you_do: Take food and hygiene supplies for yourself, your family, pets, friends or neighbors, or volunteer your time at the pantry. The group also offers nutrition education for classes and groups.

schedule.text: No set hours are listed. Come by when your schedule allows, since stock changes day to day with donations.

first_step.how: Come to the covered awning between the two entrance doors that face Stenton Avenue. No registration is needed. To volunteer, use the Get Involved page.
first_step.basis: Anyone can take items with no registration and no income check, and the site lists a clear way to volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: Visit the covered awning, where two fridges and two pantries hold food and hygiene supplies that you can take for free. Stock changes day to day with donations, so a particular item may be gone when you arrive. Groups or students can contact the pantry to arrange a session on healthy eating and food preparation.
first_visit_tips: Street parking on Stenton Avenue is limited, and the active driveway is not for parking.
The site asks visitors to be careful when opening doors on Stenton Avenue.

records.notes: The site footer and one flyer file name read 2025. Neither is used as dated evidence, so status rests on the 2025-09 CityCast article. The /get-involved/ and /volunteer/ pages returned 404, so volunteer details come from the home page. No street hours or accessibility details are published. The fiscal sponsor is in leads_only.
